name: Unexpected LLM Provider Egress
hypothesis: A workload with no approved AI dependency contacts an LLM provider or AI gateway.

name: Unauthorized Local LLM Runtime
hypothesis: A local LLM runtime or model-serving process appears on a host outside the approved AI inventory.

name: Agent Privilege Boundary Crossing
hypothesis: An agent moves from read-only or analysis context into a privileged tool action without the required authorization state.

name: RAG or Memory Integrity Drift
hypothesis: Trusted RAG content or persistent agent memory changes from an unapproved source or outside the expected ingestion path.

name: Model Artifact Provenance Drift
hypothesis: A model or serving artifact digest differs from the approved manifest or trusted publisher record.

name: AI Gateway Credential Anomaly
hypothesis: An AI gateway identity accesses, exports or uses provider credentials outside its normal administrative pattern.

name: New or Changed MCP Capability
hypothesis: An MCP server, identity or advertised capability appears or changes without an approved configuration event.

name: Agent Loop or Budget Exhaustion
hypothesis: An agent exceeds normal planning iterations, tool-call rates or budget thresholds.

name: Automated Dependency Admission Without Review
hypothesis: A coding agent or automation installs a new dependency before provenance and review controls complete.

name: Sensitive Canary in Model Output
hypothesis: A protected synthetic canary or classified marker appears in generated output.
